parameters.name: section_id

planningRules.rule: Never choose the teacher. Which teacher takes a class is the Coordinator's decision, and this call commits somebody's working week for a session.

Never work around a clash. All five conditions are refusals, not warnings (BR-3, BR-4, BR-5, BR-6) — a plan that moved to the next free period, or dropped the room to get past a double booking, has rewritten the timetable to suit itself.

Report what the assignment clashed against, by name. Told only that there is a conflict, a coordinator has to find it themselves (BR-7) — the section, the leave or the room that has it comes back with the refusal.

Report the free teachers that come back with a refusal. They are those who teach the subject and have no class, no substitute cover and no unavailability at that time (BR-8), so a replacement is chosen from a list rather than by checking teachers one by one.
Report an empty free-teacher list honestly. Where nobody is free the refusal stands, and suggesting somebody unsuitable is worse than saying so (E13).
Never assign into a slot that already holds a subject. E5 is BR-4 working; clearing the slot first is a deliberate act on a draft (BR-9).
Never treat the section as a class. A timetable is held against a section, and a request naming only a class has not said which of 5-A or 5-B is meant (BR-1).
Never describe a draft slot as scheduled for anybody. Nothing in a draft is visible to a teacher, a student or a guardian (BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It goes on the record of a change to a week that staff and families planned around (BR-11), and it is what explains the move to whoever asks.

Change only the slots the actor named. Every change reaches the teachers and families attached to it (BR-12), and a tidied adjacent period is a household told their child's week moved for no reason anybody gave.
